newsitem.title: UK: Generators' sale has not hit UK sell-offs - Treasury.
newsitem.headline: Generators' sale has not hit UK sell-offs - Treasury.

text.p: The Treasury has told a committee of MPs that Britain's privatisation programme has suffered no long-term damage from events surrounding the 1995 sale of shares in National Power Plc and PowerGen.

Small shareholders and institutions were angered by the fact that on the second day of trading after the 3.59 billion stg sale, the Director General of Electricity Supply announced a review of regional electricity companies' price controls.

Although such a review could not directly impact profits at National Power and Powergen, the share prices of the two firms were depressed for two months following the announcement, the Public Accounts Committee noted in a report.

But the report said Treasury officials had had told the committee "there had been no indications that the Director General's announcement had any long-term impact on investors' willingness to participate in further privatisations".

It said Treasury research had shown that three-quarters of the top 50 institutional investors in the generating companies had invested in the next major privatisation -- that of Railtrack Plc in 1996.
The committee said the Treasury officials had told it that ministers were consulted in the last week of the sale of the second tranche of National Power and PowerGen shares.
But they regretted in view of the embarrassment to the government that they had not been consulted a second time before it was allowed to proceed.
"We share the Treasury's regret that ministers were not consulted further before the final decision was taken by Treasury officials," the committee concluded.
